correctness.rationale: With r rounds of remaining spread, a core source reaches at most 2r-1 pendants for r≥1 and zero for r=0. A pendant source reaches its own pendant and other pendants only within cycle distance r-2, yielding at most max(1,2r-3) for r≥1 and exactly one for r=0. Thus k rounds cover at most (k-1)²+1 pendants and k-1 rounds cannot suffice. At equality each source attains its bound and the pendant footprints partition the cycle. Since the maximum arc length 2k-3 is less than n, there is no wraparound saturation ambiguity; each odd-length arc has a unique center. Rounds with r≥2 must use cores, the r=1 singleton permits either type and the final singleton must use its pendant. Conversely all such tilings cover every pendant and its core except possibly the final core; the latter has a neighboring nonsingleton block because there are only two singleton blocks and n≥5, and that block's core radius extends one further than its pendant radius. Disjoint cycle intervals of radii h_s,h_t have center distance at least h_s+h_t+1, which exceeds t-s for s<t≤k-1 with h_i=k-i-1. Pendant sources add a step for distinct indices; the last pendant lies outside every earlier footprint so its distance from any earlier core source exceeds k-s, and it is at least two steps from the penultimate source. Thus the constructed schedules satisfy even strict inequality in the stated ignition condition. A clockwise start of the first block gives n choices, arranging the other time labels gives (k-1)! choices, and the penultimate source gives the factor of two. Fixing every source but one fixes the complement footprint; its center and vertex type are forced except for the penultimate switch. This proves the matching. Every ordered schedule fixes at least three center indices if preserved, impossible for a nonidentity symmetry of the cycle, so the dihedral orbit count is (k-1)!. Inspected the supplied C++ enumeration and tiling checker without executing them. An independently written distance enumeration exhausted all 10³ triples on S₅, found 20 schedules and 10 exchange edges each of degree one at its endpoints, and found no two-round success. This corroborates only k=3.

value.rationale: The critical sizes are exactly those where the pendant capacity has no slack, making them a natural rigidity boundary. The known scalar minimum does not characterize the successful schedules. An exhaustive classification gives factorially many optima but the strongest possible fragmentation compatible with any variability: all optima have exactly one local move. This isolates the sole effect of the pendant choice on mobility and gives a baseline for testing what changes below saturation.
